svg.aria-label: DBSCAN: core, border and noise Panel: One cluster and an isolated point Panel: Counts and distance to a core One cluster and an isolated point Feature x: 1 to 6 Feature y: 1 to 5 Core (scatter): c1 C1 (2, 2); c2 C2 (2.5, 2); c3 C3 (2, 2.5); c4 C4 (2.5, 2.5) Border (scatter): b B (3.4, 2) Noise (scatter): n N (5, 4) C2 neighborhood (epsilon 1): center (2.5, 2), radius 1 C2 to B: 0.9 (inside): (2.5, 2) → (3.4, 2) C4 to B: 1.030 (outside): (2.5, 2.5) → (3.4, 2) B has only B and C2 within distance 1. It is border because C2 is core; N is too far from every core. Counts and distance to a core Nearby | Count | To core C1 · Core: C1 C2 C3 C4 | 4 | 0 C2 · Core: C1 C2 C3 C4 B | 5 | 0 C3 · Core: C1 C2 C3 C4 | 4 | 0 C4 · Core: C1 C2 C3 C4 | 4 | 0 B · Border: C2 B | 2 | 0.9 N · Noise: N | 1 | 2.915 B · Border: highlighted row Count includes self. To core is the nearest core distance (0 for cores); border needs fewer than 4 neighbors and distance at most 1. Illustrative Euclidean data: epsilon 1; min_samples 4 counts the point itself. All four core points belong to one cluster.
